archetype.name: Play-In Team (three-point volume)
archetype.definition: A team built around launching threes and crashing the glass, with enough of last season's 44-win core to hover around the middle of the East, but not yet showing the offense that made it dangerous.

report.headline: A 2-1 start covering for an offense that has stopped making shots
report.take:
Charlotte arrives at the end of its first week 2-1, tied atop the Southeast, but the record is better than the play. The Hornets have been outscored by 35 points over three games, a Net Rtg of -11.7 that ranks 25th, and the margin implies one win rather than two. Nearly all of that comes from one night: an 81-128 home loss to Atlanta, wedged between two single-digit wins over Brooklyn and Miami. Three games with one blowout in them is a tiny sample, and the honest read is that we know the shape of this team better than its level.

The shape is extreme. No team takes a bigger share of its shots from three (a 53 3PA Rate, first in the league and well above last season's 48.7), almost nobody gets to the line less (FT Rate 29th), and the misses are going in the scorebook as misses: 29.6% from three, 48.5 eFG %, a 102.3 ORtg that ranks 29th. Add a TOV % of 18, 28th in the league and far above last season's 13.5, and the offense is beating itself before the defense gets involved. What keeps it afloat is the glass: a 32.4 ORB % and 75.2 DRB % both rank in the top seven, so the volume-three approach at least comes with second chances.

The individual lines tell you where the shooting slump lives. Brandon Miller is using 34.8% of possessions on a 41.1 TS %, and Sion James has scored 6 points in 77 minutes on a 17.6 TS %. Against that, Grayson Allen (12 threes, 76.8 TS %) and Naz Reid (60 points, 12 threes) have been the offense. The frontcourt is the only group grading above a D, a B- carried by Reid, Moussa Diabaté and Ryan Kalkbrenner, and Reid is listed Day-To-Day. On-Off figures this early (Kalkbrenner +53.8, Diabaté -46.9) are mostly noise from who happened to be on the floor during the Atlanta rout.

History argues the offense is better than this. Last season Charlotte ran a 119.4 ORtg, fifth in the league, went 44-38, and actually finished nine wins below what its margin implied. A team that shot 37.8% from three on volume does not become a 29.6% team overnight. Expect the shooting and turnovers to drift back toward last year, which would turn this into a roughly break-even team; the defense, 19th by DRtg and giving up a lot of rim attempts, is what caps it.

strengths.title: Owning the offensive and defensive glass
strengths.body: Charlotte is top seven in both ORB % and DRB %, and 6th in REB %. It is the one part of the profile that held from last season, when REB % was 54 and ORB % 30.5, so it looks structural rather than a three-game fluke. With a three-heavy shot diet producing long rebounds, the extra possessions are what keep a cold offense competitive.

strengths.title: Allen and Reid carrying the scoring
strengths.body: Grayson Allen has 12 threes on a 76.8 TS % and the best on-court impact on the roster, and Naz Reid leads the team with 60 points while hitting 12 threes from the center spot. Allen's efficiency will cool, but the pair give the volume approach the shooters it needs while Miller struggles. Reid's Day-To-Day tag is the one thing that could pull this support out.

strengths.title: Finishing at the rim is hard
strengths.body: Opponents are shooting 59.8% within four feet, 6th-best in the league and well under the league's 66.2. A rotation of three centers (Reid, Diabaté, Kalkbrenner) explains it. It matters because so many shots are getting there.

concerns.title: An offense shooting and handling poorly
concerns.body: A 102.3 ORtg ranks 29th, built on 29.6% three-point shooting at the league's highest volume, the 29th FT Rate and a TOV % of 18. The shooting should come back toward last season's 37.8% given who is taking the shots, but the turnovers and the absence of free throws are habits worth watching. Until one of them changes, the offense depends on hot nights from deep.

concerns.title: Miller's inefficient high usage
concerns.body: Brandon Miller is using 34.8% of possessions while posting a 41.1 TS % and a -11.3 BPM. A slump this size in three games is likely partly noise, but it sits at the center of the wing group's D grade and of the offense's collapse. If he does not get back to efficient scoring, Charlotte has no second creator on the wing.

concerns.title: Perimeter and paint access on defense
concerns.body: Opponents are taking 35.1% of their shots at the rim (26th) and hitting 38.7% from three (25th). The three-point figure will likely regress some, but conceding both rim attempts and open looks is why the DRtg sits 19th. Wings have been the soft spot, with small forwards taking a larger share of points against Charlotte than the league norm.

trend.note: Two narrow wins around one 81-128 blowout; the record and the margin point in different directions, and three games are too few to call a direction.

weekAhead.headline: Five games, two against unbeaten Detroit, the week's real test
weekAhead.body:
It is a heavy week: five games, home and away against Washington, two against Detroit, and Philadelphia at home. Detroit is the problem. At 3-0 with a 12.7 Net Rtg, top-seven on both ends and A-level wings and frontcourt, the Pistons rebound nearly as well as Charlotte and shoot 42% from three. Two meetings with them could easily undo the 2-1 start.

The other three games are winnable but not easy. Washington (11th on the site) gets to the line more than anyone, while its defense holds opponents to 28.8% from three, a bad matchup for the league's most three-dependent offense. Philadelphia has the 5th-best defense but is last in REB %, which is exactly where Charlotte can create extra shots. A 2-3 week would be a fair outcome; 3-2 would require the shooting to wake up.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's size against Charlotte's glass
keyMatchups.body: Detroit ranks 3rd in REB % and 2nd in RPG, neutralizing Charlotte's one reliable edge. Its defense has also shut centers down (7.33 points a game to the position, the fewest in the league), which targets Reid. Oddly, it has been carved up by power forwards, giving a minutes opening to Salaün and Steinbach.

keyMatchups.title: Washington's three-point defense, free throws
keyMatchups.body: The Wizards hold opponents to 28.8% from three, 4th in the league, and lead the league in FT Rate. That pits Charlotte's three-heavy offense against a defense that contests them, and its fouling-light, rim-permissive defense against a team that draws whistles. Charlotte's edge is the offensive glass: Washington is 25th in ORB % and 18th in DRB %.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against Philadelphia
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia is last in ORB % and REB %, but it also has the league's best TOV % and a top-five DRtg. Charlotte has to win this one on the offensive boards while not giving the ball away at its current rate. Two bottom-tier offenses (PHI is 28th by ORtg) suggests a low-scoring game where possessions decide it.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Brandon Miller's shooting comes back and Naz Reid stays on the floor; without both, the volume-three offense has too few made shots to survive Detroit twice.

restOfSeason.body:
The 2-1 record and the -11.7 Net Rtg are both mostly noise at three games; last season's 119.4 ORtg and 44-38 finish, with a margin that implied considerably more wins, are the better anchor. Expect the three-point percentage to climb back toward the mid-to-high 30s and the turnovers to ease, which would lift the offense back toward the league's upper half. The rebounding looks real. What likely does not come back fully is a defense that concedes rim attempts and has never been better than middle of the pack in this stretch of history.

That adds up to a team in the 36-44 win range, fighting for a play-in or low playoff seed rather than the 55-win pace the record implies or the deep losing season the margin implies. The ORtg should settle somewhere in the 110-116 range, and the DRtg near 112-116.
swingFactors: Cutting the turnover rate back to last season's level

confidence.note: Three games, one a blowout that dominates every rate stat.
